zh: 拜占庭研究在两个层次上展开。学者只要着眼于某个具体问题，往往就能做出出色的研究。可是，一旦需要说明这个文化整体如何运作、立足于哪些基本前提、其中大多数人接受了什么样的观念，他们就依旧倚赖二十世纪三十年代形成的成见。这些成见形成的方式颇有疑问，却因为人们不加批判地反复沿用，一直延续至今。它们越传越广，俨然成了公认的事实。我们用来概括拜占庭的整套术语都属于这一类。这里列出我打算在续作中追问的几个主要概念：“皇帝”与“帝国”（能用它们来译
吗？）、“多族群帝国”（可拜占庭的罗马人究竟是什么人？），以及“普世的”或“普遍的”（学者赋予这些词的用法似乎是现代人发明的）。这些概念给拜占庭戴上了一副面具。现在该开始一层一层地揭开它了。
en: Byzantine Studies is a field that operates on two levels. Its scholars produce excellent work on any specific topic to which they turn their attention, but when they have to say something about how the culture worked as a whole, the basic premises on which it rested, and the ideologies that most of its people accepted, they continue to rely on stereotypes from the 1930s that were produced in questionable ways and that survive today because they are uncritically recycled. They acquire momentum and the status of known facts. The whole of our apparatus of general terms belongs in this category, and I list here the main ones that I intend to interrogate in the sequel: “emperor” and “empire” (do they translate

), “multiethnic empire” (but what were the Romans of Byzantium?), and “ecumenical” or “universal” (whose usage by scholars seems to be a modern invention). These concepts have placed a mask on the face of Byzantium; it is time to start peeling it off, layer by layer.

zh: 我们发明这些范畴后，又将拜占庭人借以理解自身及其在世界中位置的许多词排斥在外：“罗马人”（与“基督徒”并非同义）、“世俗”（基督教思想的基本范畴），以及本书着力讨论的、构成拜占庭人政治领域的

，也就是“共和国”。我们与东罗马人充满活力的政治文化之间，横亘着一个现代人构想出来的“拜占庭”，仿佛它就等同于神权统治和专制主义。我们之所以把他们的文化等同于其宗教，首先是因为中世纪的西方各个强权把罗马遗产据为己有，拒绝承认东方帝国同样继承了这份遗产。其次，启蒙哲人借这个想象中的基督教神权政体来思考自己的问题，无意增进对那个特定历史社会的理解。令人遗憾的是，我们至今还缺少一部拜占庭研究史，来解释昔日的成见和偏见如何成了这门学科的根基。在西方人的想象中，拜占庭扮演“专制的正教基督教帝国”这个角色已经太久，以至于很难想象它还有别的面貌。这套说法也掺进了不少东方主义。
en: Having invented these categories, we have then ostracized many of the terms by which the Byzantines understood themselves and their place in the world: “Roman” (which did not mean the same as Christian), “secular” (which is a fundamental category of Christian thought), and the one on which this book has focused, the

or “republic” that constituted the Byzantines’ political sphere. An imaginary modern construct labeled “Byzantium,” identified with theocracy and absolutism, has come to stand between us and the vibrant political culture of the east Romans. We identify their culture with its religion, first, because various western powers appropriated its Roman legacy during the course of the Middle Ages and denied it to the eastern empire; second, because having such a Christian theocracy of the imagination was good for Enlightenment philosophers to think with, for their own purposes, not because they wanted to understand that specific historical society any better. But unfortunately we still lack a history of Byzantine Studies that would explain how past stereotypes and prejudices have come to constitute the foundations of the field. Byzantium has played the role of “the absolutist Orthodox Christian empire” in the western imagination for so long that it is hard to think of it as anything else. No small dose of Orientalism has been poured into this recipe.

zh: 走出这一困境的最好办法，是重新确认拜占庭的罗马身份。古代
的规范深深植根于拜占庭政治领域的观念之中。人民主权缺少施政的制度，却体现为皇帝始终要经受的全民公决。政治就是内战的威胁。正当性就是民众的拥戴。我们所谓的拜占庭，是一个承袭罗马传统、不乏动荡、政治活跃而终究稳定的君主制共和国。在别人眼中，也在它自己眼中，它扮作了一个帝国神权政体。
en: The best way out of this predicament is to reclaim the Roman identity of Byzantium. The norms of the ancient

were firmly embedded in the ideology of its political sphere. Popular sovereignty lacked institutions of governance but found expression in the continual referendum to which emperors were subject. Politics was the threat of civil war. Legitimacy was popularity. What we call Byzantium was a turbulent, politically dynamic, but ultimately stable monarchical republic in the Roman tradition masquerading, to itself as much as to others, as an imperial theocracy.
